question: Is our support ticket data current enough to act on today?

input.purpose: Check the latest sync and latest record timestamps for the Zendesk ticket tables against the as-of date.
input.sql:
SELECT 'zendesk.ticket' AS src, MAX(_fivetran_synced) AS last_synced, MAX(updated_at) AS max_updated_at, MAX(created_at) AS max_created_at, COUNT(*) AS row_count, SUM(CASE WHEN _fivetran_deleted THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS deleted_rows FROM zendesk.ticket
UNION ALL
SELECT 'zendesk.ticket_tag', MAX(_fivetran_synced), NULL, NULL, COUNT(*), SUM(CASE WHEN _fivetran_deleted THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) FROM zendesk.ticket_tag
UNION ALL
SELECT 'zendesk.organization', MAX(_fivetran_synced), NULL, MAX(created_at), COUNT(*), SUM(CASE WHEN _fivetran_deleted THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) FROM zendesk.organization

input.purpose: Check ticket volume by day over the last 30 days to see whether recent tickets are landing, and confirm the current date in the database.
input.sql: SELECT CAST(created_at AS DATE) AS created_day, COUNT(*) AS tickets, MAX(_fivetran_synced) AS synced_max FROM zendesk.ticket WHERE created_at >= TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-10-01 00:00:00+00' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1 DESC LIMIT 100

input.purpose: Look at the distribution of sync timestamps in the ticket table and whether any ticket timestamps are after the as-of date.
input.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n, MIN(_fivetran_synced) AS min_synced, MAX(_fivetran_synced) AS max_synced, COUNT(DISTINCT CAST(_fivetran_synced AS DATE)) AS distinct_sync_days, MAX(created_at) AS max_created, MAX(updated_at) AS max_updated, SUM(CASE WHEN created_at > TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-11-06 23:59:59+00' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS created_after_asof, SUM(CASE WHEN updated_at > TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-11-06 23:59:59+00' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS updated_after_asof, SUM(CASE WHEN _fivetran_synced > TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-11-06 23:59:59+00' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS synced_after_asof FROM zendesk.ticket

input.purpose: Compare freshness of the other systems (carrier, SAP, Salesforce) to see whether the sync stamps are uniformly ahead of the as-of date.
input.sql:
SELECT 'carrier_pg.shipment' AS src, MAX(_fivetran_synced) AS last_synced, MAX(updated_at) AS max_business_ts FROM carrier_pg.shipment
UNION ALL SELECT 'carrier_pg.shipment_event', MAX(_fivetran_synced), MAX(event_at) FROM carrier_pg.shipment_event
UNION ALL SELECT 'sap_s4.likp', MAX(_fivetran_synced), NULL FROM sap_s4.likp
UNION ALL SELECT 'sap_s4.vbak', MAX(_fivetran_synced), NULL FROM sap_s4.vbak
UNION ALL SELECT 'salesforce.account', MAX(_fivetran_synced), MAX(last_modified_date) FROM salesforce.account
UNION ALL SELECT 'salesforce.opportunity', MAX(_fivetran_synced), MAX(last_modified_date) FROM salesforce.opportunity

answer.answer_summary: No. The support ticket data is not current enough to act on today. The newest ticket was created 3 Nov 2026 and nothing has been created or updated since, even though the prior month averaged about 7 tickets a day, so the Zendesk feed appears to have stopped. The sync timestamps say the data was loaded on 9 Nov, which is after today's date, so they cannot be trusted to confirm freshness.

metrics_used.definition: MAX(created_at) and MAX(updated_at) on zendesk.ticket, compared with the as-of date of 6 Nov 2026

metrics_used.name: Daily ticket volume
metrics_used.definition: Count of zendesk.ticket rows by created date, 1 Oct to 3 Nov 2026 (234 tickets over 34 days, about 6.9 per day)

metrics_used.definition: MAX(_fivetran_synced) on zendesk.ticket, used only as a secondary check

lineage: zendesk.ticket -> ticket volume and recency checks (no downstream model identified)
zendesk.ticket_tag and zendesk.organization checked for sync recency only

freshness.source: zendesk.ticket (latest business timestamp: created 2026-11-03 16:33 UTC, updated 2026-11-03 18:00 UTC)
freshness.last_synced: 2026-11-09 19:47 UTC (recorded sync stamp, after the as-of date)
2026-11-09 19:47 UTC (recorded sync stamp, after the as-of date)

freshness.source: carrier_pg, sap_s4 and salesforce tables (for comparison only)
freshness.last_synced: 2026-11-11 16:13 to 18:28 UTC (recorded sync stamps, after the as-of date)

assumptions: The as-of date of 6 Nov 2026 is correct. Today's date is treated as 6 Nov, so the 9 Nov and 11 Nov sync stamps are read as impossible, not as real loads.
Zero tickets on 4 and 5 Nov (Wednesday and Thursday) are not normal, given the roughly 7 tickets per day average for October.
Ticket created and updated timestamps are the more reliable freshness signal, because the sync stamps are dated after the as-of date.
caveats: The sync stamps are dated 9 Nov for Zendesk and 11 Nov for the other systems, which is after today's date. Either the warehouse clock is wrong or the timestamps are unreliable. I could not verify when the load actually ran.

There may be no real tickets for 4 to 6 Nov. Support volume could have dropped sharply, but a three-day gap against a steady baseline is much more likely to be a feed problem. The source system (Zendesk) should be checked directly.
Only 3 tickets were created on 3 Nov, and the last one was at 16:33 UTC, so that day may be partial in the feed too.
I did not check whether the carrier, SAP or Salesforce feeds have a similar gap, because my question was about support tickets only.

explanation.title: Counted cancelled deliveries
explanation.detail: The SAP tables keep 310 cancelled deliveries as soft-deleted rows (_fivetran_deleted = true). This query never filters them out, so cancelled deliveries count as late.
explanation.sql_line: UNION ALL SELECT 'sap_s4.likp', MAX(_fivetran_synced), NULL FROM sap_s4.likp

explanation.title: Missed a customer split across two CRM accounts
explanation.detail: Halbrook Fluid Systems has a look-alike duplicate account ("… GmbH") with no SAP number. Two of its open shipping tickets sit on the duplicate, so the customer looked healthy.

explanation.title: Read every history row of the account tier
explanation.detail: salesforce.account keeps one row per version of each account (history mode). Without filtering to _fivetran_active, accounts that changed tier appear twice, and Quenmere Paper Mills GmbH still looks Strategic.
explanation.sql_line: UNION ALL SELECT 'salesforce.account', MAX(_fivetran_synced), MAX(last_modified_date) FROM salesforce.account
